after: Deploying pathology models through separate scripts makes preprocessing, spatial sampling and previous analysis settings difficult to inspect. This project develops ZY-Path, a local PyQt5 desktop application that connects supported PyTorch CPU inference to explicit Single image and Tiled analysis controls, spatial inspection, recorded history and export, with a separate supervisor-provided segmentation integration. The classifier achieved 90.68% accuracy and 88.59% macro-F1 on 7,180 native 224 × 224 CRC-VAL-HE-7K patches through the application’s default Pillow core, agreeing with every predicted label from the recorded reference pipeline. The 19 October Windows baseline passed 370 automated tests; the current-source Linux/offscreen-Qt run passed 504 tests with one genuine segmentation-weight availability failure and no errors. The engineering contribution is a model-aware desktop workflow with explicit crop geometry, independent task semantics and reproducible parameter restoration. UAT, final-version manual Windows acceptance, systematic performance measurements and clean-machine deployment remain incomplete.

The application loads and runs PyTorch models on CPU; no OpenVINO conversion or runtime is implemented. The genuine classification checkpoint occupies 1,726,089 bytes (1.646 MiB). Its checksum is recorded in Appendix E.1. A segmentation file-size measurement has not been supplied, and there is no converted-model size to report. Structural compatibility permits supported model representations, not arbitrary task or label semantics.

The augmentation order and parameters are reproducible from the training script: Resize(224, 224); VerticalFlip(p=0.5); HorizontalFlip(p=0.5); HueSaturationValue(hue_shift_limit=(-25, 0), sat_shift_limit=0, val_shift_limit=0, p=1); Rotate(p=1, border_mode=cv2.BORDER_CONSTANT, value=0); RandomSizedCrop((224, 224), 224, 224); and ToTensorV2 followed by float conversion. Arguments not explicitly set use the defaults of the recorded Albumentations 1.3.1 environment. Because the crop height range is fixed at 224 after resizing to 224 × 224, this crop operation does not provide evidence of training with different source fields of view.

Class weights are calculated as w_c = 1 − n_c / Σ_j n_j from the training counts; they are not inverse-frequency weights. Cross-entropy uses a summed reduction, with epoch reporting normalised by the accumulated class-weight denominator. The script seeds Python, NumPy, PyTorch and the data-loader generator with 42, seeds workers from their PyTorch worker seed, disables cuDNN benchmarking and requests deterministic cuDNN behaviour. Continuation restores the model, optimizer and scheduler states. The reported results describe this recorded run; no multi-seed training-variation study was conducted.

location: 3.3.4 Explicit classification modes and crop geometry
before: Source crop dimensions determine the field of view before resampling to 224 × 224. The dataset’s nominal source-patch dimensions and resolution are documented in Section 4.2.6. The interface retains 512 × 512 as an editable starting value; its physical-scale equivalence to the training data is unverified for an arbitrary uploaded image. The evaluation consequences are discussed in Section 4.5.3.
after:
Source crop dimensions determine the field of view before resampling to 224 × 224. At the source dataset’s nominal 0.5 μm/pixel, a 224-pixel edge spans 112 μm. If a new raster’s resolution r is known in μm/pixel, a candidate crop edge covering that field is approximately 112/r pixels; this is a physical-scale calculation, not evidence of optimal predictive performance. The interface retains 512 × 512 as an editable starting value. Values such as 256 and 300 are exploratory source-crop candidates, while the network input remains 224 × 224. A controlled comparison should keep the crop centre, source image, model, backend and display dimensions fixed. No outcomes from those new-size trials are supplied here.

Ordinary Run Inference snapshots the current preference width, height and resize backend at launch. Restoring a history result does not replace those new-run defaults. Re-run alone supplies the recorded parameter snapshot, and the input summary returns to current preferences when it finishes. A change made while inference is active applies to the next run. The 11-case preference-lifetime regression verifies actual crop boxes, recorded geometry, same-value re-entry, mode/image changes, clear view and parameter isolation.

location: 3.3.8 History schema, artifacts and rerun isolation
after: Clear view removes the current input, visible result and session metadata and clears history selection. It does not delete saved analyses or source files. Clear Selection, Esc in the history table and a click on empty table space can leave no row selected. Restoring history also synchronises the left-side original-image thumbnail; the completed record retains its own identity independently of subsequent model selections.

PdfExportWorker snapshots the selected result, metadata, map and export options before background generation. Progress and cooperative cancellation keep the GUI responsive; the destination is atomically replaced only after a complete report is written. Standard PDF quality is the default: report display copies are sized for up to 300 DPI, large photographs and overlays use high-quality JPEG, and class maps use nearest-neighbour resizing with lossless encoding. Original resolution retains full image pixels with lossless encoding. Text, numerical tables, predictions, saved masks and source files are unchanged. The report distinguishes original image dimensions from display-copy quality and an export-time file checksum from an identity actually recorded at inference.

The inference panel’s built-in/custom selector is a session choice. Selecting the built-in model clears the visible local-model filename while remembering that local choice for a later explicit return in the same session. This does not change either task’s saved startup default or relabel the completed result’s Session metadata. Interrupted custom validation is resumed when required rather than leaving a stale loading state.

Tile boundaries and optional one-based tile numbers are drawn in source coordinates. Selecting a tile in an image or its detail row locates the same numbered crop and displays its original pixels, rectangle, label and confidence. The Square action copies the current width to the height once; dimensions remain independently editable. Numeric preference controls route wheel input to page scrolling. The expandable resize guide explains the available backends without changing the model or network input size.

Linked panning updates the peer view without repeatedly recentering the actively dragged pane. Resizing retains the intended source-coordinate centre, and divider dragging uses a rubber-band preview before the panes resize on release. Fractional wheel deltas produce proportional zoom while zero or horizontal-only deltas do not trigger an unintended zoom. These operations affect presentation and leave analysis values unchanged.
